task_language: put the black bowl on top of the cabinet

subtasks.name: pick(black_bowl)
subtasks.outcome: success: side/rim grasp with the hand rotated ~90 deg, lifted by ~180

subtasks.name: place(black_bowl, cabinet_top, on)
subtasks.outcome: failed: bowl carried near the cabinet but held over the open bottom drawer area until timeout, never released

behaviour_summary: pi0 grasps the bowl, brings it to the cabinet's right edge at ~200, then drifts back and hovers holding the bowl above the open bottom drawer / beside the cabinet from 220 to 409 without lowering or releasing it.
runs_trained_task: libero_10 KITCHEN_SCENE4: put the black bowl in the bottom drawer of the cabinet and close it (partial: carries bowl toward the open bottom drawer but never commits)

failures.mode_definition: After a successful grasp, the policy carries the object and hovers near (but never over) the instructed destination, often drifting toward a trained-task destination, without lowering or releasing it until timeout.
hl_remedy: HALT once the EE has been near-stationary for 3 frames with the object held
REPROMPT 'put the black bowl on top of the cabinet'
WATCH 3 s for the EE moving over the cabinet top ROI; retry once, then ESCALATE
failures.prevention: Coordinator marks the trained destination (bottom drawer) as a distractor and the FR agent watches that the carried object's EE path ends over the instructed destination ROI.
failures.observation: At 200 the bowl is near the cabinet's right top edge; at 220 it moves back right over the open bottom drawer, and from 220 to 409 it is held at roughly the same height in front of/right of the cabinet, never over the cabinet top and never lowered into the drawer either. Gripper stays closed on the rim throughout.

notes: Unclear whether pi0 is torn between the trained destination (bottom drawer) and the instructed one (cabinet top) or simply cannot reach a stable height above the cabinet; the bowl never goes above the cabinet top surface. Grasp is unusual (hand rotated sideways) but holds.
